applies_why: The judge text applies the stating-verse inquiry to a pressed link by asking whether the pressed texts state the contrary in their own words rather than weighing the chains by footing.
quote: UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē states no verdict on the begetter in either direction, and the defender answered Luke 1:27, Luke 2:4 and Numbers 1:2 in [CR2] section A.3 and [CR3]; the verb change is real [L1]/[L2] but neither text's own words state the other reading's contrary.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: the phrase 'that no one of them states the contrary in its own words': I weighed (1) reading it as a retired own-words-contrary test the judge cannot use, against (2) reading it as merely barring a standalone verse from deciding while permitting a note that no single verse states the contrary; the first reading controls because the judge uses that absence to leave the link underdetermined.
why: The judge leaves the link UNDERDETERMINED because neither text's own words state the contrary, which is the verse-by-verse stating-verse test K-C retires.
